text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TRUD

-- Bulgaria's cabinet began debating a once off tax payment which would allow individuals and firms to legalise undeclared assets acquired in the last seven years in a move to boost budget revenue, government officials said.
The draft envisages that Bulgarians with undeclared assets pay 20-25 percent tax without having to declare their origin.
-- Germany's Westdeutche Algemeine Zeitung said it had raised its stake in Bulgaria's biggest private 168 Hours Pressgroup to 100 percent from 70 percent.
-- Deputy of the ethnic Turk Movement for Rights and Freedoms Yudzhel Atila resigned from parliament because of personal problems.

-- Bulgaria's parliament is expected to change the heads of the state national radio, the national television and the official news agency BTA, said Ekaterina Michailova, a deputy from the ruling Union of Democratic Forces.

-- Bulgaria's Dobrich City court postponed ruling on an insolvency suit filed by the Bulgarian National Bank against the private Dobrudzha Bank for September 30, after the BNB asked for an additional investigation of a capital raise announced by the Dobrudzha bank in April, a court official said.
Dobrudzha Bank was placed in receivership in September 1996.
-- Bulgaria hopes to join the Central European Free Trade Association by the end of the year, deputy Trade minister Ivan Dimitrov said.
24 CHASA

-- Bulgaria is expected to cut its conscription army service to 12 months from 18 months for high school graduates and to nine months from 12 months for university graduates in a move to curb budget spendings.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet lifted a $2,000 annual limit on purchase of currency for personal use on the domestic market following introduction of a currency board system on July 1, Finance minister Muravei Radev said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet appointed Bulgarian National Bank governor Svetoslav Gavriiski as country representative in the International Monetary Fund, the government press centre said.
STANDART
-- Foreign firms have invested some $307 million in Bulgaria in the first six months of this year, the newspaper said quoting Deutche Welle radio said.
PARI
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would cut its simple main annual interest rate to 9.56 percent from 10.12 percent.
NOVINAR
-- Bulgaria's former communist leader Todor Zhivkov said he would publish his memoirs. Zhivkov is expected to raise the curtain on his ousting in 1989.
